title: U.S. House · Florida's 2nd District
area: The eastern Florida Panhandle and the Big Bend region, including Panama City to Tallahassee.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Neal Dunn did not make the ballot in the August 18, 2026 Republican primary, which Austin Rogers won with 30.3% in an eight-candidate field. Amanda Green won the Democratic primary with 33.4% over three opponents.

candidates.name: Amanda Green
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 33.4% over three opponents.

summary.text: Amanda Green is the Democratic nominee for the open Florida 2nd Congressional District seat. A Florida State University alumna who studied international development, economics and public administration, she has worked for a decade in operations and pricing roles supporting global health programs.

background.text: Studied international development, economics and public administration at Florida State University.
Began her career with a USAID partner organization.
Worked for about a decade as an operations director and pricing expert supporting global health programs, famine monitoring systems, and relief efforts in Ukraine.

priorities.text: Addressing the affordability crisis by supporting farmers, lowering housing costs, banning corporate ownership of single-family homes, and protecting Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid and veterans' benefits.
Restoring accountability in government by banning congressional stock trading and enacting term limits.
Holding regular in-person and virtual town halls with constituents.

positions.summary: Says she will protect Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid and veterans' benefits as part of addressing the affordability crisis.

candidates.name: Austin Rogers
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary with 30.3% in an eight-candidate field; incumbent Neal Dunn withdrew before the primary and is listed by Ballotpedia as a withdrawn candidate.

summary.text: Austin Rogers is the Republican nominee for the open Florida 2nd Congressional District seat, having won a crowded primary after incumbent Neal Dunn did not advance.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia biography, Candidate Connection survey, or accessible campaign-site content could be located for Rogers as of research date; only his primary election results were confirmed.
